claims.text: High-temperature calorimetry can accurately determine the melting temperature of high-entropy alloys.
High-temperature calorimetry can accurately determine the enthalpy of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
High-temperature calorimetry can accurately determine the entropy of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
High-temperature calorimetry can accurately determine the volume change at melting of high-entropy alloys.
High-temperature calorimetry can accurately determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method can determine the listed properties efficiently.
The proposed calorimetry measurement operates from 298 to 2000 K at a heating rate of 10 K/min.
An argon or helium atmosphere prevents oxidation during the measurement.
Crystal structure and chemical composition mediate the response of the alloy to the calorimetry measurement.
Heat flow and temperature changes during melting and solidification are measured directly.
The method is expected to determine melting temperature within 5 K of the actual value.
The method is expected to determine enthalpy of fusion within 5% of the actual value.
The method is expected to determine entropy of fusion within 5% of the actual value.
The method is expected to determine volume change at melting within 2% of the actual value.
The approach applies to high-entropy alloys having mixing entropy of at least 1.5 R and maximum solute content of 35 at.%.
Heat-flow and temperature measurement uncertainty may affect the results.
Interactions between an alloy and the calorimetry apparatus may affect the results.
Deviation of more than 10 K in melting temperature and more than 10% in enthalpy of fusion relative to existing methods would falsify the approach.

contradictions.description: The predicted accuracy is within 5 K and 5% for melting temperature and enthalpy, but the approach is falsified only beyond 10 K and 10%; results between those limits would violate the prediction without meeting the stated falsification rule.
